newsitem.title: USA: Furon, Medex sign $160 mln merger.
newsitem.headline: Furon, Medex sign $160 mln merger.

text.p: Furon Co said on Wednesday it signed a definitive agreement to merge unit, FCY Inc, with Medix Inc in a deal valued at $160 million.

FCY will offer $23.50 a share for all Medex's outstanding common stock, which puts the offer at about a 59 percent premium to the stock's average trading price over the last 30 days. Medex is up 7-3/4 to 23 following the news.

Furon plans to acquire any remaining Medex shares at the same price as paid in the tender offer, when the offer has ended. The merger deal and offer have been approved by the boards of directors of each company. Medex would be required to pay an $8.0 million break-up fee in some circumstances.

Medex Inc, based in Hilliard, Ohio, makes polymer-based critical care products and infusion systems for medical and surgical use that are sold in over 50 countries. In its fiscal year ended June 1996, it generated sales of $99.3 million.

"Medex has excellent channels to market directly to health care providers," Michael Hagan, Furon chief executive said in a statement. "From this base, we can accelerate growth with new products, product line extensions and market penetration."
Furon makes polymer components for products in a number of industries including health care. It had sales of $345 million for its fiscal year ended February 3, 1996.
